title: Choose the Meetings & Tasks workbench
question: Which structure should carry the meeting-to-completion workflow?

options.label: Twin Registers
options.thesis: Meetings and tasks remain distinct ruled registers joined by one focused record pane.
options.viewport: A compact date rail leads into parallel meeting and task registers, with the selected record expanding into a shared working pane.
options.risk: The parallel registers require disciplined density to avoid feeling like two unrelated modules.

options.label: My Commitments
options.thesis: The employee's next actions lead; meetings appear as the source and evidence behind each commitment.
options.viewport: A due-now commitment queue owns the first view, with selected task detail, meeting origin, comments, and attachments arranged beside it.
options.risk: Meeting organizers may need one extra step to reach agenda and minutes authoring.

options.label: Decision Chain
options.thesis: Every agenda item visibly resolves into a note, decision, or assigned task so follow-through never loses its origin.
options.viewport: A meeting register opens into a vertical agenda trace where decisions and assigned tasks branch directly from each discussed item.
options.risk: The trace is exceptional for meeting work but less efficient for scanning unrelated tasks across many meetings.
